#1712. Are you ok, Noni?

Arsenal’s squad construction has given them a lot of depth and diversity in terms of profiles. Timber and White for right-back, Calafiori and Hincapie for left-back. Ezri Konsa has, incredibly, offered both protection and threat to the impregnable Saliba and Gabriel partnership. Bruno and Lewis Skelly, Rice and Zubimendi and Odegaard and Merino for midfield.

Eze and Tzolis for the left-wing. Havertz and Gyokeres for centre-forward. Of course, some of these pairings are more symbiotic than others. Mosquera is probably going to fall behind Konsa as a back up to either one of Saliba or Gabriel. In reality, Zubimendi is only going to play ahead of Rice if Rice is injured or Arsenal have a nice easy game against League Two opposition, for example…

On the face of it, Noni Madueke should really be in that third layer of the squad with Mosquera, Kepa and where Zubimendi probably now resides. The role of back-up to Bukayo Saka ought to have been one with limited opportunity. In a sense, I was always a little surprised that Madueke signed up for it when he came to the club from Chelsea last summer.

I was slightly surprised that Arsenal spent so much money on a player who was always incredibly unlikely to dislodge Saka no matter how much he improved. And how much scope was there going to be for Madueke to get the sort of rhythm and consistency of selection to hone his talents?

Now I strongly suspect that Arsenal would have had anxieties over Saka’s ability to stay fit after tearing his hamstring in December 2024 and missing a few months of football. It was the first significant injury Saka had incurred and after quickly deciding that loanee winger Raheem Sterling was not going to be an adequate replacement, they amended for his absence with a blend of 17-year-old Ethan Nwaneri and surplus left-back Kieran Tierney.

It isn’t difficult to see how Arsenal viewed the right-wing spot as a single point of failure but encouraging Madueke to see it as an attractive position must have challenged even Mikel Arteta’s powers of persuasion. Yet just over a year on from signing for Arsenal, Madueke has a league title winners medal (‘while others are tweeting and posting’) with 25 starts to his name last season, 16 of which were in the Premier League.

In reality, being Bukayo Saka’s third leg has, to this point, proved to be a savvy career move for Madueke because he is getting plenty of time on the pitch in Saka’s increasing absences. This extends to the England National Team too, where Madueke plays the same role. But it was a role that still earned him four starts for his country in a World Cup, including a start in the quarter-final against Norway.

A Premier League title winners medal, a Champions League Final appearance and four World Cup starts was not a bad return for Madueke in terms of playing time. I think we knew when Arsenal bought him that Noni was a talented but phlegmatic player, relentless in taking on his full-back but the quality of his end-product could vary markedly.

In his new signing profile of Madueke on Arseblog, Phil Costa wrote, ‘there’s a feeling that Arsenal lack penetration from their wingers (Bukayo Saka aside); chaos factor, some unpredictability, and Madueke brings this in spades. His first thought when receiving the ball is centred around provoking defenders and driving towards goal, which means you can isolate him without too much focus on the overall setup – you just wind him up and let him go.

‘There are two specific metrics to love when assessing the 23-year-old; per FBRef data, he currently sits in the 95th percentile for progressive carries (6.82 per 90) and the 98th percentile for carries into the box (4.12 per 90). Those are big numbers.’ There was never any doubt about Madueke’s ability to get the ball into threatening areas, the question has always been what he does when he gets there.

Last season, some clips of him harumphing the ball out of the stadium on his right foot went semi-viral. I also think some of his performances were impacted by a lack of balance in the front three. With technicians like Havertz and Odegaard unavailable, he was often playing alongside fellow blunderbusses like Gyokeres and Martinelli.

I admit that my tolerance for inefficiency is high when it comes to attackers. I think attacking is a volume game. The vast majority of attacks come to nothing, the vast majority of shots do not go in or even work a goalkeeper. Individual attacks are the weather but, overall, attacking is the climate. The more you do it and sustain it, the more likely you are to score.

So my ‘we can fix him’ gene for slightly wayward wingers is high. I didn’t even mind Gervinho (a frustrating player, no doubt, but the Bradford miss has become the defining image of his Arsenal career which I don’t believe was fully representative of his performances).

The video of Madueke’s right foot ballooning the ball into the upper tier against Kairat last season has been refined. Both his goals this season have been on his right foot, particularly notably against Nottingham Forest where he cut in on his right and unleashed a low and controlled shot. It might have taken a helpful deflection but that’s because he kept the attempt low.

Last season, his right footed efforts were more in danger of colliding with low flying aircraft on their way into orbit. Noni’s goal against Slavia Praha demonstrated his pace in behind. It was the sort of goal and chance Gabriel Martinelli was hoovering up in Europe last season. European games tend to offer more space in behind and with Martinelli gone, Madueke is one of the few Arsenal attackers explosive enough to exploit it.

Indeed, in my view, he ought to have won Arsenal a match winning penalty in Budapest against Paris Saint Germain in May. There are signs of greater maturity and efficiency in his game. According to WhoScored.com his pass success rate in the Premier League last season was 76.2%. This season so far it is 86.3%.

I think he has learned that he does not have to go for the full-back at 100mph every single time he gets the ball and has varied his game. In the Champions League game against Lille, he sent 15 crosses into the penalty area, having sent six into the area in the game before against Leeds. 15 crosses sounds like a lot but it was very clearly under instruction from Mikel Arteta.

After that Lille game, the manager said of Madueke, ‘I said when you talk about players being ‘clinical’, sometimes that means scoring five in every 100. It’s about generating volume, more actions and getting him into the good positions, because he will decide matches. He had a really big contribution a few days ago, today he had a contribution in the last final pass as well.’

Being omitted from the England squad in September, according to Arteta, provided additional motivation for Noni, ‘After the break, he is showing something else, another level of anger, another level of conviction as well as in his actions and he is becoming decisive in matches, which is what we expect from a player like him.’

He has now been omitted from the England squad again for the November international round. It is a decision I don’t really understand from Thomas Tuchel but I am happy if it continues to provide Madueke with an additional reason to fine tune his game and because it hopefully protects a player who has become very important.

I admit I am not entirely sure how good Madueke is going to be in, say, three years’ time. He is 24 and it’s at that age that attackers typically start to increase their decisive actions. He has Max Dowman in the rearview mirror too. I think Madueke has a really high ceiling and there are small, but encouraging, signs of improvement.

#1711. Newcastle star Amar Dedic sparks six-car police swoop after being spotted with a BOW AND ARROWS in Northumberland beauty spot before weapon is seized

Published: 13:29 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 17:28 EDT, 5 November 2026

Newcastle United star Amar Dedic was at the centre of a major police operation after he was spotted carrying a bow and arrows at a Northumberland beauty spot – with at least SIX patrol cars involved in the search for the £30million defender.

The Bosnia international sparked alarm when a concerned member of the public reported seeing him and a friend walking with the weapon near a reservoir in the countryside outside Newcastle.

Police dispatched marked and unmarked vehicles to the area in Harlow Hill, with some understood to have been armed response units, before Dedic and his companion were finally intercepted around seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate.

Sources have described the dramatic swoop on Dedic's vehicle before officers searched the car and seized a bow and arrows, with the 24-year-old questioned about his activities.

In a bizarre twist, Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett arrived at the scene while police were speaking to Dedic. It is understood the pair were in the area by chance and stopped to offer assistance.

After speaking to the two men, officers were satisfied there was no threat to the public, with police subsequently stating that the equipment was believed to have been intended for recreational use.

Amar Dedic played in Newcastle's 1-0 defeat by Everton on Monday evening

Dedic was spotted with a crossbow off Military Road, the 61-mile B6318 in Northumberland

However, enquiries remain ongoing into the incident, which happened on Wednesday afternoon. It is understood that Dedic and his friend had fired some arrows while in the countryside, although it remains unclear what they were aiming at. Hunting any animal or bird with a bow and arrow or crossbow is illegal in the UK.

Dedic joined Newcastle from Benfica during the summer and has impressed at right back despite the club's difficult start to the season.

Daily Mail Sport understands he will not face disciplinary action from Newcastle over the incident, although there is a feeling that the player was naive to believe he could walk around the countryside carrying such weaponry.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson said: 'Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area.

'Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows. At this stage, it is understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Enquiries are ongoing.'

Dedic is expected to be available for Saturday's Premier League trip to Fulham, where Newcastle will attempt to halt a run of four defeats in five matches across all competitions.

That’s exactly what we need, that’s what we’re signing, that’s the type of player that can help us to make the difference and he certainly did that during the night.

#1709. Diego Simeone explains Raphinha and Robert Lewandowski difference

By Naim Beneddra | 07 Nov 2026 14:47

Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone has admitted that Barcelona have become more difficult to defend against following Hansi Flick's decision to deploy Raphinha in a central attacking role rather than Robert Lewandowski.

The Brazilian has enjoyed an extraordinary start to the 2026-27 campaign, scoring 19 goals in just 13 appearances, and his new position has given Atletico a different problem to solve ahead of Sunday's top-of-the-table La Liga showdown.

Barcelona travel to the Metropolitano with a two-point advantage over Simeone's side, who can move above the defending champions with a victory.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference on Saturday, the Argentine identified Raphinha's movement as the most significant tactical difference between the Barcelona side he faced last season and the one preparing to visit Madrid.

While Lewandowski offered a more conventional presence inside the penalty area, Raphinha's tendency to drop into midfield and attack different spaces has complicated the defensive task.

Simeone has never concealed his admiration for Raphinha, having repeatedly praised the former Leeds United winger's intensity, movement and attacking output.

The Atletico boss was again full of praise for the 29-year-old on Saturday, describing him as an exceptional footballer whose influence has continued to grow since moving into the centre of Flick's attack.

"For me, he's an extraordinary footballer, with his work rate, pace, goals and assists," Simeone told reporters.

"He had an incredible season last year and he's started this one brilliantly, playing in a different position where he's also doing very well and giving his team plenty of options."

However, it was the comparison with Lewandowski that provided the clearest insight into the challenge facing Atletico.

Simeone insisted that Barcelona's overall approach remains largely unchanged, with Flick continuing to demand aggressive pressing, a high defensive line and quick recoveries of possession.

The difference, he explained, lies in the profile of the player leading the attack.

"Lewandowski was more of a positional number nine," Simeone said.

"Raphinha can appear as an attacking midfielder to link the play. Gordon is now on the left and he's doing very well.

"They've lost the more positional reference point they had with Lewandowski, and now it's potentially more complicated to defend against them, because dealing with Raphinha isn't the same as dealing with a number nine, regardless of how dangerous he is inside the box."

The Barcelona captain's movement creates decisions for opposition defenders that were less frequent when Lewandowski operated as the central striker.

Following Raphinha into deeper positions can open space behind the defensive line, while allowing him to receive the ball between the lines risks giving Barcelona an additional player in midfield.

Simeone specifically highlighted that flexibility when discussing how his team would approach Sunday's encounter.

"The difference is Raphinha's positioning, which changes some of what they were doing last season because of his movement, his ability to create numerical superiority in midfield and his runs in behind towards the end of attacks," he explained.

Those qualities have helped Raphinha thrive alongside Anthony Gordon and Lamine Yamal, with the two wide players offering further attacking options around the Brazilian.

Raphinha's performances have provided emphatic support for Flick's decision to change his position.

The former Leeds winger has scored 15 times in La Liga this season, making him the division's leading goalscorer ahead of Sunday's meeting.

His record against Atletico also gives Simeone reason to pay particular attention to him.

Across 10 previous meetings with the Madrid club, Raphinha has been on the winning side eight times, drawing once and losing just once.

He has contributed two goals and six assists in those encounters, establishing himself as a frequent source of problems for Atletico's defence.

His absence proved significant during last season's cup competitions, when Barcelona were eliminated by Simeone's side in both the Copa del Rey and Champions League.

Raphinha missed the first leg of the Copa del Rey semi-final, which Atletico won 4-0, before scoring in Barcelona's 3-0 second-leg victory.

He was also unavailable for both legs of their Champions League quarter-final defeat.

This time, the Brazilian is available, although his recent fitness problems have raised questions about whether he is operating at full capacity.

Simeone, meanwhile, has acknowledged the scale of the challenge facing his side.

"We're playing against a very good team, possibly the best. I have no doubt about that," the Atletico manager said.

"We know we're going to suffer for large parts of the match. Hopefully, we can play the game we have in mind."

Atletico have won nine of their opening 11 league fixtures, but their task on Sunday is particularly demanding given the attacking form of the visitors.

Barcelona, who lead the standings with 30 points to Atletico's 28, will be looking to extend their advantage at the summit.

Simeone's men, meanwhile, have an opportunity to take control of the title race, provided they can find an answer to the movement of the player their own manager has identified as Barcelona's biggest tactical difference.

The Argentine has explained why Raphinha presents such a difficult problem. Sunday's contest will reveal whether Atletico have found a way to contain him.

#1708. Arsenal 1-0 Hull: Not efficient, but enough

In yesterday’s preview blog, I spoke about Arsenal’s attacking efficiency, and how that might be key to taking all three points. In yesterday’s game against Hull, Arsenal took 21 shots, 10 of which were on target, and scored one goal from that. Efficient?

Despite generally dominating possession, I thought there was a lack of precision in certain aspects of our first half play. Passes weren’t quite quick enough or accurate enough, but there were moments when we could have found the breakthrough. Gabriel almost got on the end of a Noni Madueke cross which was flicked on towards the back post, Rice had a tame shot from a free kick before a late header which he probably should have done better with.

And then there was Kai Havertz. It’s fair to say Hull didn’t leave a lot of room behind a defensive line that often had six players stretched across it, but late in the half a superb Martin Odegaard pass sent him clean through, one on one with the keeper. I haven’t seen replays but in real time I felt like he should have pulled the trigger – instead he over-complicated it. You have to be prepared to shoot from there, even if it’s on your wrong foot.

Then there was a penalty incident when he complained vociferously, play went on, the ref was then told to go to the screen and we all assumed it would be a penalty. However, the ref said it was a foul but Havertz was offside – and it felt like a massive waste of time. Afterwards, it emerged it should have been a penalty, but apparently the rule is ‘open to interpretation’. So clear as mud then.

In the second half, we seemed to play down our right a lot, with Madueke the outlet most of the time. I thought he did pretty well, much better than Christos Tzolis on the other side, but the breakthrough wouldn’t come. Mikel Merino replaced Rice (who seemed to be on the end of a wild challenge in midfield that the ref just ignored as he tumbled through the air), and Viktor Gyokeres came on for Havertz.

On 71 minutes though, we found the goal. Madueke’s shot was spilled by the keeper, Odegaard was quickest to react to poke the ball home for 1-0. And to be fair, you always felt confident that would be enough. We are the masters of the single goal margin win, and this was another one. Not a day that will live long in the memory or anything, but a 1-0 win that takes us into the Interlull in really good shape, and there’s not much arguing with that.

Or really, much more to say about this game. Mikel Arteta sounded happy enough, saying:

I’m delighted with the win. To go into the international break with a win is one of the best things about being a coach or player, I would say. Regarding the performance, I thought we were the better team, had enough chances to score and make it bigger for ourselves and we weren’t efficient enough to take them.

We then had to rely on generating volume, plenty of persisting until we finally broke them down. Martin then got the goal. Not the most beautiful one, but the most effective one, a simple ‘shoot and then follow the next action’, and that was ultimately enough to win the game.

So Arsenal sit top of the table, with 9 wins from 10 so far this season in the league, and it’s a very impressive run of form. Do I wish we had more attacking potency? Absolutely, and I do worry a bit that it might bite us in the arse somewhere down the line, but for now, we can see that this is a team that just knows how to win, and perhaps that’s the most important thing.

Right, I’m gonna leave it there for this morning. I have to head back to Dublin today. It was great to see lots of you over the weekend, until next time! And we’ll have an Arsecast Extra for you tomorrow too.

#1707. Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:

He is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the new season.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

#1706. Leeds 1-0 Tottenham: Roberto De Zerbi sets unwanted 39-game worst as Premier League record exposes major Spurs flaw

By Lewis Nolan | 07 Nov 2026 15:20

Tottenham Hotspur's loss to Leeds United means they have failed to win any of the past 39 matches in the Premier League in which they conceded first (D9, L30), an unwanted record in the competition.

Spurs were hopeful of securing a fourth consecutive win in the Premier League, but they instead suffered a 1-0 defeat at Elland Road, with Noah Okafor scoring a late winner.

The result leaves the Londoners in 10th place with 12 points after 10 matchweeks, but they are only three points from 16th-placed Coventry City.

Roberto De Zerbi will be particularly concerned by his team's failure to find the back of the net after going behind, with the club having only scored 10 times in the top flight so far.

Opta data shows that Spurs have in fact failed to win any of their last 39 Premier League games in which they conceded first, their longest ever run in the competition.

39 - Tottenham Hotspur have failed to win any of their last 39 games in the Premier League in which they've conceded the opening goal (D9 L30); their longest ever run in the competition. Setback. https://t.co/0FfwlLIXO1

Though Leeds could have been reduced to 10 men in the first half, a possible VAR error should not distract from the fact that Spurs looked poor offensively yet again.

The Londoners produced seven shots to the victors' 16 on Saturday, and no player in the visiting team produced more than one shot on target.

Despite signing the likes of Omar Marmoush and Savio in the summer transfer window, De Zerbi's side have rarely offered any threat in the final third.

James Maddison's creativity has been missed, but his absence cannot explain why they have failed to score in half of their Premier League games this season.

Spurs have finished 17th in the Premier League in each of the last two seasons, so nobody at the club can afford to take safety for granted.

Tottenham could end the weekend in 14th place, and the gap to the bottom three could be as small as two points.

De Zerbi has not been able to eradicate all of the defensive mistakes that have plagued the Londoners, and given his players have frequently struggled in the final third, it would not be surprising if they battled against demotion yet again.

#1705. Press not dealt with and unexploited spaces: Tactical analysis of AC Milan 0-2 Ferencvaros

AC Milan suffered a disappointing defeat against Ferencvaros on Thursday evening, and as highlighted in our tactical analysis, a lot went wrong for the Rossoneri.

Milan’s Europa League campaign has turned into somewhat of a nightmare, after being tipped to fight for the title in the summer. Just one win in the first four games means a top 8 finish is very difficult, while there are no guarantees for the playoffs either.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ruben Amorim certainly voiced his disappointment after the game, sending a clear message to the players, even if the head coach deserves some of the blame too. Below is the tactical breakdown from Rohit Rajeev, who has pointed out several flaws.

Ferencvaros were committed to pressing Milan and looked to create numerical overloads in the wide spaces. In this particular sequence, Milan found themselves in a 6v8 situation, highlighting the numerical disadvantage they faced when trying to play out from the back.

In the centre, Musah was very isolated as Bartesaghi, Cisse and Hutchinson failed to drop short or move inside to make themselves available. This left the American with limited options and made it easier for Ferencvaros to sustain their press and disrupt Milan’s build-up.

Individual errors also made things difficult for Milan when going forward. In the example below, Terracciano failed to play a simple pass into Hutchinson’s path, preventing Milan from launching a counter-attack.

As Ferencvaros were pressing high and maintained a high defensive line as a result, there was space to exploit in behind. However, Milan failed to make runs behind the defence, while very few long balls were played to target that space.

The lack of depth in their attacking movements allowed Ferencvaros to remain compact, leaving little room between the lines for Milan to exploit. It also meant that Ramos was very isolated up front, with effectively a 3v1 created against him.

The first goal that Milan conceded stemmed from two individual errors. De Winter made a poor decision by playing the ball back to Torriani, while the goalkeeper’s heavy first touch didn’t exactly make things any better in stopping the danger.

Milan then pushed forward in search of an equaliser and their defence was reduced from three players to two. Ferencvaros won possession after De Winter’s clearance, launching a quick counter-attack.

Joseph then made an intelligent run to block Bartesaghi’s path, preventing him from recovering defensively.

Taking a look at Milan’s first half, it was characterised by sterile possession as there were significantly more passes in their own half as opposed to the opponent’s half. Ferencvaros also dominated the physical battles, winning every ground duel and breaking up any attacking rhythm for Milan.

#1704. Crisis-hit FIFA chief Gianni Infantino 'requested VIP treatment for his daughters and their dogs at Miami airport'

By DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER

Published: 09:47 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EDT, 5 November 2026

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is facing more uncomfortable questions after it emerged that his office asked for 'VIP treatment' for his daughters and their pet dogs on a trip from Miami to Qatar.

Infantino's future has been under the microscope after a scandal-laden few months, with honorary Japanese FA president Kohzo Tashima announcing on Thursday that he will stand against Infantino in next year's presidential election.

On Thursday, The Times revealed that back in May, Infantino's presidential office wrote to Miami airport officials asking for someone to 'assist' three of his daughters - and their pets - through security for a personal trip to Qatar.

Miami airport's VIP protocol reportedly allows diplomats and other special guests to be escorted through security checkpoints up to the door of the plane. Officers can also request early boarding.

These privileges are not automatically laid on for loved ones traveling separately, with protocol stating that 'courtesies... will not be extended' to family members of VIPs 'when the families are traveling on their own.'

But according to documents reviewed by the Daily Mail, members of Infantino's family enjoyed the airport's services dozens of times while traveling without the FIFA president between 2024 and 2026.

Gianni Infantino's office reportedly requested 'VIP treatment' for his daughters and their dogs

The FIFA president's future has been under the microscope after a scandal-laden few months

In a statement to The Times, Miami airport insisted these requests are dealt with 'on a case-by-case basis.' The Daily Mail has contacted FIFA for comment but a spokesperson told The Times: 'Port courtesy requests were made to Miami international airport (MIA), on the advice of a former adviser to the Fifa president.

'Port courtesies are provided at no charge to the president of Fifa given his position as the head of an association or NGO. Mr Infantino’s family members are also entitled to request these services under MIA’s own Courtesies of Port Handbook and these are also provided free of any charge, on a case-by-case basis, at the discretion of MIA.'

Infantino's position is already under threat heading into FIFA's presidential election next March, when he is hoping to be elected to a fourth term. Back in December, Infantino awarded Trump the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize – to widespread ridicule.

During the World Cup, the Balogun affair saw Infantino accused of favoritism and caving to the White House, while the FIFA president and Trump were mocked for handing over the trophy to Spain together.

Before long, Infantino faced a mutiny over his secret plans – later scrapped – to sell a stake in the World Cup to private equity investors including Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.

Then earlier this week, FIFA strongly denied allegations that Infantino influenced Trump administration officials to fast-track a work permit for his undocumented Nicaraguan housekeeper after she lost her legal status, according to bombshell documents.

The global soccer chief is alleged to have turned to politically-connected contacts to secure a new work permit for Yajarlin del Socorro Fernandez after the White House revoked her legal permission to work in the United States, according to documents reviewed by the Daily Mail.

#1703. Arsenal transfer news: Mikel Arteta reveals "valuable" role amid Antonio Nusa links to Gunners ahead of January window

By Lewis Nolan | 07 Nov 2026 15:22

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has revealed that international matches are used to help assess potential transfer targets amid links to Antonio Nusa.

The RB Leipzig winger has often been touted as a possible target of the Gunners, especially as the Londoners have at times looked blunt in the final third.

With the international break beginning after this weekend, the 21-year-old will be back in action for Norway, and he will play alongside Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard.

Speaking to reporters ahead of their Premier League clash with Hull City on Saturday, Arteta insisted that international matches can be informative when making transfer decisions, saying: "Yes, we do [use international football to aid work ahead of a transfer window].

"Obviously, when we have the opportunity to talk to our players about some players that they share two or three weeks together with, it's very valuable information. I think we all do that. It is a big difference between the Premier League and international football and what is there, but there's always a lot to learn."

Nusa has been included in the Norway squad for his nation's games against Wales on November 14 and against Demark on November 17, and perhaps Odegaard could help convince the winger to move to the Emirates in that time.

Nusa is enjoying a strong season in Germany, with the winger currently Leipzig's leading scorer (six) and assist provider (seven) in all competitions.

His return in both categories have already surpassed the five goals and four assists he produced in 2025-26, and his pace has proven deadly when cutting inside onto his right foot from the left flank.

It is rare for an attacker to be as strong at finishing as they are at creating chances, so Nusa's profile could be invaluable against deep defences.

While he is likely to be expensive in either the January or summer transfer windows, Arsenal should have him high on their radar.

Arsenal have at times been criticised for their style of play, with opposition fans and pundits arguing that they lack attacking intent.

However, it should be remembered that Arteta does not have a particularly elite set of forwards to choose from, with there question marks about every attacker's place in the lineup.

While Nusa may take time to settle into the Premier League, the prospect of Arsenal improving their frontline should be a worry for the rest of the division given the Gunners are already one of the best defensive teams in the world.

#1701. Nottingham Forest vs. Man City lineups confirmed: Delap, Yates, O'Reilly, Anderson decisions made

By Oliver Thomas | 07 Nov 2026 16:22, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 16:37

Enzo Maresca has made a total of three changes to his Manchester City starting lineup for this evening’s Premier League clash against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground.

Captain Ruben Dias, Josko Gvardiol and Jeremy Doku all began as substitutes for City’s 3-2 Champions League win at RB Leipzig on Wednesday, but they have all returned to the first XI to face Forest.

Nico O’Reilly – who is ‘not 100% fit’ and has been left out of the latest England squad – drops down to the substitutes’ bench along with Matheus Nunes and Phil Foden.

Abdukodir Khusanov and Gvardiol will begin as full-backs, with Dias and Marc Guehi linking up at the heart of the defence in front of under-fire goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Elliot Anderson starts in midfield at the City Ground for the first time since his £116m move from Forest to City in the summer, with the England international – who turned 24 on Friday – starting alongside Enzo Fernandez.

Doku will start in his favoured left-wing position, forcing Iliman Ndiaye to move over to the right flank, while Rayan Cherki continues in the number 10 role behind striker Erling Haaland, who is without a goal in his last four appearances against Forest.

As for Nottingham Forest, under-pressure head coach Oliver Glasner has made just two changes to the side that began the 2-0 defeat at Brentford last weekend.

Captain Ryan Yates is handed his first start of the season, with the midfielder replacing Dan Ndoye, while Daniel Munoz is fit to start and comes in for Ola Aina at right wing-back.

Yates is expected to start in the middle of the pitch alongside Xaver Schlager and James McAtee, with the latter potentially given the license to roam further forward to link up with Morgan Gibbs-White.

Despite failing to score in each of his last five starts, ex-City youngster Liam Delap retains his place up front, with Chris Wood – yet to start at PL game this season – Igor Jesus and Arnaud Kalimuendo all on the substitutes’ bench.

Munoz and Neco Williams will provide the width in Glasner’s side as wing-backs, while Murillo, Nikola Milenkovic and Jair Cunha will continue in a three-man backline protecting goalkeeper Matz Sels.

Nottingham Forest starting lineup: Sels; Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo; Munoz, Schlager, Yates, McAtee, Williams; Gibbs-White; Delap

Subs: John Victor, Diomande, Sangare, Hudson-Odoi, Wood, Igor Jesus, Ndoye, Kalimuendo, Netz

Manchester City starting lineup: Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Fernndez; Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku; Haaland

Subs: Rulli, Kovacic, Reis, Nunes, Bouaddi, O'Reilly, Allan Elias, Foden, Lewis

#1699. Virgil van Dijk is spot on: Liverpool's brittle defence leaves them looking like a vulnerable mess - it is unsustainable and MUST be fixed, writes LEWIS STEELE

Published: 12:00 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 17:38 EDT, 5 November 2026

Liverpool's defensive woes are not sustainable, insists skipper Virgil van Dijk who says the team cannot accept losing in the way they did at Fenerbahce.

The Reds lost 3-2 having twice led in Istanbul, with individual errors and lapses in concentration costing them.

Andoni Iraola’s men have now suffered back-to-back defeats after also losing to Arsenal – and they have conceded three goals in each of their last three European games, against LASK, Villarreal and Fenerbahce.

When this statistic was put to Van Dijk, he said: ‘(Our defending) is definitely not sustainable. That’s why it is a very disappointing night, for many reasons but definitely the goals we conceded and the manner we conceded them as well. There is work to do.

‘It is very, very tough. Three set pieces as well. We have been very good at them so far this season but we switched off and were not ready for the first and second balls. Yeah, it is a tough one to take.

‘I mentioned after the last game, we as a group have to go through good moments but also lesser good moments. That will only form a bigger bond, it will be only beneficial.

Liverpool suffered a disappointing 3-2 Champions League loss to Fenerbahce on Wednesday

Captain Virgil van Dijk insisted Liverpool's poor defending is not 'sustainable' after the game

‘No one wants to lose games especially how we did today but it should only help us in the near future. We should not accept losing, especially in the manner we did today.’

Asked if he was angry, the Dutchman said: ‘Yes. But I didn’t show it today because everyone looked disappointed and they have a reason to be, they should be disappointed. We cannot lose in the manner we did today. But we did that and it is down to Fenerbahce as well.’

Van Dijk is right. The defence has been all over the place at times this season – especially in Europe.

Iraola thought he had won the game with a masterstroke triple substitution just after the hour mark when Cody Gakpo assisted Alexander Isak two minutes after the pair joined Florian Wirtz in entering the field.

But in trying to win the game – which is commendable – Iraola left the back door open. It felt ajar all night as Fenerbahce continually had joy down the flanks.

Van Dijk was asked if the deafening atmosphere of the Istanbul crowd played a part and said: ‘It is very difficult for everyone on the pitch because you can’t communicate easily.’

That could be an excuse but these players are world class and cannot put too much blame on the atmosphere.

Jeremy Jacquet has been imperious since joining from Rennes but the Frenchman had his first bad game in a Liverpool shirt, while Van Dijk was not too much better.

Milos Kerkez (above) and Kostas Tsimikas are proving a serious problem at left back

September 9: Liverpool 2-1 Atletico Madrid

Alisson, too, has left questions to be asked over his performances of late. After giving the ball away cheaply for Arsenal’s winner on Sunday, he was at fault for Fenerbahce’s decisive goal by dilly-dallying over whether to come for a cross. He should have gobbled it up.

But the real problem is at full back. Milos Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas are not good enough – not now, anyway. That should be first on the priority list in future transfer windows.

Ronald Araujo, rested on the night, was missed.

The approach of ‘you can score, we will score more’ has been used – intentionally or not – in most European games this term. When it comes off, as it did in 6-3 and 4-3 wins over LASK and Villarreal respectively, it is exciting.

When it doesn’t, Liverpool just look a vulnerable mess. Work to do for Iraola ahead of a trip to Selhurst Park and Crystal Palace on Sunday, where Pierre Sage is fighting for his life.

#1697. Report: Arsenal to spoil Liverpool's January transfer plans

Liverpool have a weakness at left-back, that has become clear this season.

The partnership of Milos Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas is not working for Andoni Iraola.

Neither player has stepped up to make the left-back position their own, and news that Liverpool are exploring potential replacements in January will not come as a surprise.

Several other positions also need addressing in the winter window, but left-back is a growing priority for the Anfield recruitment team and multiple players are being linked with Merseyside moves.

One such player is reportedly Barcelona's Alejandro Balde, but Arsenal may be about to spoil Liverpool's transfer plans.

Arsenal exploring Balde dealThe Barcelona left-back has been touted as the solution to all of Liverpool's problems, with former teammate Ronald Araujo thriving under Iraola early in the season. The Spaniard could look to recreate Araujo's success and make the move to Merseyside, but Premier League rivals Arsenal are reportedly also eyeing up a move. According to a report from Ekrem Konur, the Gunners could propose a swap deal that would see Balde head to London with Piero Hincapie heading the other way.

#1696. Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

“He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

Michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

“It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”

“It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a big season ahead.”

“It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”

“We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have big season and hope to win a trophy.”

All over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

Fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

Two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. His attempt is blocked and the ball, ultimately, falls at the feet of Lacey whose shot is blazed high over the bar.

There have been plenty of good things for Carrick to take from this match. The passing, while not of the standard of a cut-and-thrust Premier League match, has been good for the time of year, and there have been enough flashes of brilliance/class/invention etc to suggest that pre-season is moving in the right direction.

Lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

Both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

Maguire has had a good game. He’s played a number of long passes from the back and looked assured. This time he’s up in the PSG half and decides to have a pop - his shot testing Safanov, who saves well.

Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

Chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

Tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off

Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

The paces quickens and the game is much better for it. Mbuemo drives toward the PSG box, he cuts inside from the right before unleashing a shot that is bound for the back of the net before a fine one-handed save by Safanov. Credit, too, for Maguire whose long ball from the back found Mbuemo brilliantly. Promising...

Lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

Slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

Having seen Mount limp off in the first half, there’s more worry at the start of the second and Heaton is force off with what looks like a hamstrung injury. He dashed off his line to clear a ball and in doing so has tweaked something. Mee replaces him.

Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

And that is it for the first 45 minutes. PSG took the early lead, but from that moment on United have been the better side and deservedly are level through Mbueno’s goal.

There will be one minute of added time at the end of what has been a good first half for Man Utd.

Amad has a go from outside the box forcing the save from Safanov. He’s such a live wire and one of the best in his position in the top flight. Him or Antony? No contest, strange it took United a while to work that one out.

Yet more good work from the underrated Amad. He again closes down well on the right before winning back possession and cutting the ball back for Lacey. To think he was starring for Sunderland in the Championship while Antony was starting for United...

United have been the better side since conceding earlier and, as if to illustrate my point, as I typed that an Mbuemo free-kick is well saved by Safanov. That was heading for the top-right bin.

Great work on the left by Dorgu and Shaw ends with the latter chipping the ball to the back post where Amad is lurking with intent. The Ivorian looks to head the ball home, but before he can get anything on it it looks as though he’s pushed in the back. United players are sure it’s a penalty but, more importantly, the referee doesn’t.

Amad does brilliantly, winning the ball off Koukaba in the final third, from there he scampers toward the box before playing in Mbuemo who takes one touch before firing in a shot into the bottom right corner of the net.

Free-kick for PSG on the right, near the final third. The ball comes in and it’s straight into the arms of Heaton in the United goal.

Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

United continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

Worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

Foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

Heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

United are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

United seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

Good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

Bright start to say the least from the French side. They work the ball left and it’s an easy cross from Dro Fernandez for Mbaye to tap home for the very early lead.

They’re under way in Sweden. United are in their new vibrant red kit and PSG in their blue, red and white kit. Big fan of the French side’s kit, it harks back to the kit they had in the 1990s when the likes of George Weah and David Ginola were entertaining in the capital of France.

Man Utd: Heaton, Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw, Mount, Santos, Dorgu, Lacey, Amad, Mbeumo; Subs: Heath, Mee, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Yoro, Fernandes, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Tielemans, Zirkzee

Paris St-Germain: Safonov, Pacho, Zabarnyi, Koukaba, Boly, Beraldo, Dro, Mayulu, Kvaratskhelia, Ayari, Mbaye; Subs: Marquinhos, Mendes, Lucea, Vitinha, Neves, El Nay, Idder, Drame, Bourdin, Ndjantou, Meite, Longoni, Chevalier

And here’s a famous match that took place there, giving a certain Sir Alex Ferguson his first European trophy.

“Get a bit sharper, get better on the ball, go up a notch.”

“It’s not about today it’s about preparing. Some players have played 90 minutes, some have played three games, some have just come back. So it’s about keeping working on things we’ve been working on.”

“They’re similar to us, but have fewer senior players available . They’ve had a great time and great squad so whoever on the pitch it will be a test.”

A hugely talented player for a number of clubs, including United, who ever really lived up to his early promise.

Good to have you back, lads 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/3EgkXLqcQm

📃 Le onze de départ pour cette rencontre de préparation face à Manchester United. #PSGMUN pic.twitter.com/LodcDM1Yrm

I expect they’ll make an appearence at some point.

Ready to face PSG in our latest pre-season test ✊

Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

Bradley Barcola has waved away concerns about his transfer fee and insisted that he is not trying to replace Mohamed Salah at Liverpool.

Winger Barcola will hope to score his first Premier League goal of the season, particularly after he received criticism for his performance against Arsenal on November 1.

Boss Andoni Iraola inherited a dysfunctional team, but while he has improved the Reds from a defensive perspective, he is unlikely to get Liverpool into a title fight unless he can find a way of extracting more from the club's most expensive assets.

#1691. Liam Rosenior says Chelsea sacking had 'nothing to do with football' as he raises questions about 'tolerance' in England in first revelations about being axed just three months into the job

Published: 06:37 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EDT, 5 November 2026

Liam Rosenior has claimed he was treated unfairly during his doomed 106 days in charge of Chelsea, and that the way it ended in disaster had ‘nothing to do with football’.

Rosenior was relieved of his duties after losing five consecutive games without scoring. The fifth defeat in that run – a 3-0 loss at Brighton in which Chelsea did not even muster a shot on target – saw the players accused of downing tools to get rid of their head coach. He lasted 106 days in total.

However, Rosenior, now manager of Paris FC, who are fourth in France’s Ligue 1, has claimed his Stamford Bridge sacking was 'nothing to do with football' in a cryptic comment about 'tolerance' in English football.

The 42-year-old Englishman took aim at ‘the media’ in particular as he said in an interview with So Foot: ‘It was the best experience of my life, and the hardest, too. It was fantastic, even though it only lasted four months. I don’t want to go into details now. I’ll talk about it one day, when the time is right. But in a country where tolerance is an important value, what happened there has nothing to do with football.’

Pressed to explain, Rosenior continued: ‘I know, I answered without answering it. Actually, the moment that worried me the most was at the beginning, when we went through that five-game winning streak.

Liam Rosenior was seen passing a note to Alejandro Garnacho with Chelsea 8-2 down on aggregate against PSG - and the reaction to it clearly still rankles with him

Then-Chelsea manager Rosenior was compared to The Office star David Brent online

‘Any club would have been happy with such a run, but not Chelsea. You get good results and you’re in the spotlight. Then, there was a kind of snowball effect in the media.

‘They made fun of those instructions I gave (Alejandro) Garnacho on a scrap of paper when we were down to 10 men against PSG (during the second leg in March as they lost 8-2 on aggregate).

'The clothes I wore became a joke, the way I spoke, too. I’m not a joke! You’re the first people I’m talking to about this, and probably the last for a long time, but one day, I’ll tell you what really happened.’

It is unclear whether by ‘the media’, Rosenior meant those reporters who covered the club or social media, where he was routinely mocked and referred to as ‘LinkedIn Liam’.

Those within the actual Chelsea pack who attended Rosenior’s press conferences believe he was treated kindly despite the Blues boss not helping himself at times.

For example, his decision to suddenly drop Robert Sanchez for Filip Jorgensen backfired, especially in their Champions League last-16 first-leg loss away at PSG. When Jorgensen was then injured, Sanchez returned to the starting line-up with his confidence having been dented.

Rosenior also created a stir when he argued with a member of Arsenal’s support staff for encroaching in Chelsea’s half during their warm-up before the second leg of their Carabao Cup semi-final. He accused his opponents of breaking the ‘etiquettes in football’ afterwards.

After his players huddled around the referee Paul Tierney in the centre circle before a Premier League loss to Newcastle, Rosenior defended their pre-match routine. He described it as being designed to ‘respect the ball’ – words which were also ridiculed on social media, even if that idea did originate from Willie Isa, Chelsea’s hire from rugby league.

The former Strasbourg manager is now enjoying life back in France as manager of Paris FC

Rosenior added in his interview that he was never accepted in the Premier League, saying: ‘In England, there’s this preconceived notion of what a Premier League coach should be, how he should behave. You have to conform to that standard. People who know me know that I’m someone who tries to be sincere and authentic.

‘But I don’t have control over how the media describes me or talks about me. What I’ve understood now, and this is important for all coaches worldwide, is that social media, or the media in general, can dictate public opinion about the quality of a player or a coach.

‘This isn’t new, of course, but the biggest lesson from my time at Chelsea is knowing that they are also capable of constructing the entire narrative around a club’s trajectory.’

#1687. Opinion: Richard Hughes has left Liverpool but his transfer mistakes remain

Richard Hughes was in charge of Liverpool's transfer business during their most expensive window ever.

Last season, the Englishman spent over £450 million to try and improve the Reds' ranks.

Most people thought this amount of spending would set them up for the next few years but, in reality, that was far from the case.

Alexander Isak and Jeremie Frimpong were constantly injured with Florian Wirtz often failing to live up to expectations.

The same issues followed Liverpool into the 2026-27 season where he spent another £150 million trying to resolve those same issues.

However, now that he's gone, fans are hoping for change but, unfortunately for them, Hughes' mistakes have remained.

Liverpool are still having to suffer with having a trio of veterans among their ranks thanks to Richard Hughes

Although Hughes may have felt like he did a good job as Liverpool's sporting director, it feels like he's actually managed to make the team worse in some ways.

He handed two new long-term deals to Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai who have both been poor and, he attempted to replace Mohamed Salah with a £123 million deal for Bradley Barcola.

On the face of things, these may have felt like the right things to do at the time, but, now that we're a few months into the 2026-27 season, it's clear that they weren't.

His failure to offload some of Liverpool's benchwarmers is also beginning to hurt the Reds.

Wataru Endo, Kostas Tsimikas and Federico Chiesa are all still at the club despite not having a regular role with the Premier League outfit for some time.

And, while Julian Ward could end up generating a little bit of cash thanks to their sales, both Endo and Tsimikas' contracts expire at the end of the current season which means they're likely to leave for nothing.

But, until then, they're just taking up valuable squad spaces which has left the Reds a bit stuck.

Julian Ward needs to get Liverpool's first-team squad back to its best

Although Liverpool's performances are down to Andoni Iraola, the vast majority of their recruitment falls onto Ward's shoulders.

He was appointed as the Reds' new sporting director after Hughes chose to leave his role and, since then, several players have been linked with a switch.

The Reds may be one of the most well known football teams in the world but, that doesn't mean that they have an endless amount of money to spend.

However, with how much damage Hughes has done to their squad, it's clear that so many areas of it will need to be upgraded.

Without Liverpool doing this, they could get left even further behind their title rivals which is why it's so important for Ward to get the squad back up to scratch.

Here's hoping that Ward and Iraola can solve Liverpool's issues and get them back to where they need to be.
