Arsenal took the Premier League trophy with them to Dublin on Wednesday night and it is on show today at the Emirates. They kick off the defence of their crown on opening night against newly-promoted Coventry is just under two weeks.

Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀

When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:

“I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

#1664. Why Crystal Palace vs. Liverpool is key for Andoni Iraola's tenure amid Arne Slot comparisons before Premier League clash

By Lewis Nolan | 07 Nov 2026 23:24

Liverpool will take on Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park on Sunday, and a third consecutive defeat would place Andoni Iraola under pressure.

The head coach has so far taken charge of 15 games as Reds boss, and while he has only lost three times, there is growing discontent in some sections of the fanbase.

After losing against Arsenal in the Premier League last weekend and suffering a defeat away to Fenerbahce in the Champions League on Wednesday, there are concerns his position could be in danger if he was to suffer a third consecutive loss on Sunday.

Iraola is also only contracted to Anfield until 2028, so the Merseysiders will have to make a decision about whether to renew his deal sooner rather than later.

Heading into the upcoming international break on the back of three defeats would no doubt place Iraola under further pressure from those that were already sceptical about his appointment.

Here, Sports Mole explains why Iraola could come under extra scrutiny this weekend, while also exploring whether he should be fearful about his future at Liverpool.

One of the reasons that some Liverpool supporters are uneasy about the inconsistencies of the team this season is that they saw the club experience a turbulent 2025-26.

Under the direction of Arne Slot, the Reds finished fifth with just 60 points, and they lost 19 times in all competitions, though their 2025 Community Shield loss takes that number to 20.

Fans were distraught that Liverpool could surrender their Premier League title so easily, and the team's struggles last season created a rift amongst many, with the two camps split over their support of Slot.

The Dutchman's dismissal in May was met with mixed reactions, and the appointment of Iraola was divisive given he was replacing a title-winning manager.

While many fans have acknowledged that the squad the current head coach inherited was flawed, those that backed Slot believe that Iraola has not been held to the same standards as his predecessor.

Liverpool have 15 points so far after nine matchweeks, which is exactly the same tally as they had accumulated after the end of matchweek nine in 2025-26.

However, the Reds claimed just 45 points from their final 33 league games under Slot, with the club fortunate that they won their first five games of that campaign.

The underlying numbers in 2025-26 were alarming, and their final 33 matches extrapolated over a full season would equate to just 52 points, enough to finish 10th last term.

Iraola's side are highly unlikely to be as poor over the remainder of 2026-27, and he deserves the chance to take the squad as far as he can.

Liverpool struggled throughout Slot's final season when pressing, with critiques made of the Dutchman's out of possession approach, as well as fitness conditioning.

Iraola was highly regarded at Rayo Vallecano and Bournemouth for the intensity he demanded from his players, and that same high-energy system has been used at Liverpool to great effect.

The Reds have pressed the likes of Arsenal, Brentford and Bournemouth exceptionally well this term, and they have also looked far more assured at the back.

Liverpool have kept four clean sheets in their past seven league matches, while only conceding once against each of Brentford and Arsenal.

Manchester City may have beaten the Merseysiders 3-0 in early October, but they only managed to open the scoring once Ryan Gravenberch had been sent off.

The introduction of Ronald Araujo has been vital, with the defender essentially acting as a third centre-back at right-back, though the system that the team uses is far more structured without the ball in general

Liverpool were one of the worst clubs in the Premier League last term out of possession, so for the Reds to have improved so significantly in such a short period of time has been impressive.

Despite the undeniable improvements defensively, questions have been raised about how Iraola is platforming the team's attack given the club have scored just 11 goals in the Premier League so far.

Striker Alexander Isak has netted six times in the top flight, though he has had little service so far, and he has performed remarkably well to reach that figure.

The Reds have three £100m attackers in their squad in Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola, with the latter two yet to score in the league this season.

Portions of the fanbase have suggested that Iraola has failed the team's attackers, and considering goals are more eye-catching than defending, the team's struggles in the final third have been more apparent than the development at the other end of the pitch.

However, the head coach cannot be faulted for many of team's difficulties given he inherited Wirtz, who has never shown that he is capable of regularly producing in front of goal.

Liverpool's full-backs on both flanks have offered little threat when going forward regardless of personnel, and the only creative wide player in the squad is winger Rio Ngumoha.

The 18-year-old cannot be expected to play every game, so that has often resulted in blunt performances in attack, and the Merseysiders may not improve offensively without further investment.

Every game requires context before analysing, and even if the Reds lose against Palace on Sunday, it would be harsh to suggest that Iraola should be under pressure.

He has taken over a dysfunctional squad with several gaps, and it would be unfair to argue that he must overcome all of those problems without further transfer windows.

A Liverpool defeat on Sunday would unfortunately amplify his critics, and the November international break could be a long one for the head coach.

Victory for Iraola could take his side as high as fourth, and it would also be the club's 10th triumph in 14 games, a more than respectable return.

#1663. Only six wins in 26 games: Davide Massa will officiate Milan’s encounter with Genoa

The experienced Davide Massa has been appointed to the game between AC Milan and Genoa, set to officiate his 27th game involving the Rossoneri.

Milan desperately need to pick themselves back up after what was an embarrassing mid-week display, losing by two goals to nil against Ferencvaros at San Siro. They could have had a better opponent up next, though, as Genoa have been in red-hot form lately.

Four wins in the last five games speaks for itself and the game will be played at the Marassi as well, not San Siro. In short, this could be a difficult one for Ruben Amorim’s men, also judging by the referee who has been appointed to the game.

The referee in question, as stated in the intro, is Davide Massa. He’s one of the most experienced referees in the league but certainly hasn’t seen eye to eye with Milan in the past, even if there was no real controversy last season.

In fact, there was a 50-50 foul just before Milan’s equaliser in the second game, but Massa opted not to blow the whistle.

#1662. Club Leon vs CD Guadalajara - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 07 Nov 2026 23:56, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 18:04

Club Leon host CD Guadalajara, known as Chivas, in the Liga MX Apertura 2026 at Estadio Leon (Nou Camp) on Monday.

Leon sit ninth on 22 points in the Liga MX Apertura table after Friday's matches and need results to hold a top-eight place, while Chivas are already through to the quarter-finals on 29 points and are chasing the top seed with America and Cruz Azul level on the same total.

Leon have 22 points from 15 matches, built on six wins, four draws and five defeats, with a goal difference of only +2 from 22 scored and 20 conceded.

That leaves La Fiera ninth after Friday's round, level on points with eighth-placed Tijuana, who hold a better goal difference of +3, with Monterrey one point behind on 21 and Pumas and Queretaro on 20.

Javier Gandolfi's side have gone two matches without a win, drawing 1-1 with Toluca at home on October 24 and then losing 2-1 at Cruz Azul on November 1, where Andres Montano converted a 56th-minute penalty, Jose Paradela added a second in the 72nd minute and Jose Alvarado replied only with a stoppage-time penalty.

The 3-5 home defeat by America on October 17 is the clearest warning for this fixture, because it belongs to a run of nine goals conceded in the last five matches, in which Leon have scored every time, eight in total, and won only once, 2-0 at Tigres on October 20.

Leon won both league meetings with Chivas in 2025 at the Nou Camp, 2-1 on January 28 and 1-0 on July 19, and the fixture has not ended level at Estadio Leon since November 2016, but the most recent meeting was a 5-0 defeat at Estadio Akron on March 18.

Gandolfi said after the Cruz Azul defeat that Liguilla qualification depends only on his own team, and the arithmetic backs him up: a win would take Leon to 25 points, a draw to 23, and a defeat would leave them on 22 before the final-round trip to Santos Laguna.

Chivas have 29 points from 15 matches, with eight wins, five draws and two defeats, and their 14 goals conceded is the lowest total in the league, against 25 scored.

Gabriel Milito's side have won three in a row, 1-0 against Necaxa on October 20, 1-0 at Monterrey on October 24, where goalkeeper Raul Rangel saved a penalty, and 4-2 against Atlante on October 31, after a four-match winless run in which they collected three points from 12.

The Atlante win was led by 18-year-old Santiago Sandoval, who scored twice as a false nine after Milito left Angel Sepulveda and Ricardo Marin on the bench, with Efrain Alvarez adding one of his own and Diogo Bagui scoring an own goal.

Sandoval made his Liga MX debut as a substitute against Leon on July 19, 2025, scored both goals against Tigres in the Clausura quarter-finals, and he now has five league goals this tournament, level with Roberto Alvarado and Marin.

Chivas are the only team in the league without an away defeat, with three wins and four draws from seven road matches for 13 of 21 points, and both of their defeats this tournament came at the Estadio Akron.

America, Chivas and Cruz Azul are level on 29 points, with America ahead on a goal difference of +15 against Chivas' +11 and Cruz Azul's +10, and Chivas close the regular season at home to Cruz Azul on November 22.

Leon have no new injury concerns, although Jose Ramirez and Santiago Londono have been left out of Gandolfi's plans, while Luis Valadez (foot injury), and Angel Estrada (fractured tibia) are not available.

Juan Guevara is one yellow card from a suspension, which matters for a back line that has conceded 20 goals, and Sebastian Vegas is also reported to be on four bookings.

Gandolfi is expected to keep the side that started at Cruz Azul, with Panama international Ismael Diaz, Edgar Guerra and Alfonso Alvarado leading the attack.

For the visitors, Miguel Tapias remains in rehabilitation and Miguel Gomez has returned to treatment after a muscle relapse.

Luis Romo returned to the starting lineup against Atlante after a biceps femoris injury suffered on Mexico national-team duty, and Jose Castillo, Brian Gutierrez and Angel Sepulveda are back in contention.

Milito is expected to stay with the lineup that beat Atlante, although Marin, who has five league goals, and Sepulveda are the options if he restores a nominal striker in place of Sandoval's false-nine role.

Garcia; Moreno, Romana, Guevara, Mora; Echeverria, Rodriguez, Arcila; Guerra, A. Alvarado, Diaz

Rangel; Campillo, Romo, Aguirre; Ledezma, Govea, R. Gonzalez, B. Gonzalez; Alvarez, R. Alvarado, Sandoval

The gap in the numbers points towards Chivas, who average 1.67 goals per game against a Leon defence that concedes 1.33, while Leon must break down a Chivas back line that has conceded only 14 goals and kept six clean sheets.

Leon have scored in each of their last five league matches and won both previous league meetings at the Nou Camp in 2025, so a goal for the hosts is likely, but they have taken only five points from their last five games and conceded in 11 of their 15 matches, and we expect Chivas to score twice and leave Leon needing a result at Santos Laguna on the final day.

#1660. Martin O'Neill tells Celtic to keep believing they can reach Europa League knockouts after stirring revival

Published: 18:27 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 18:45 EDT, 5 November 2026

Martin O’Neill urged his Celtic side to focus on making it to the knockout stage of the Europa League after a second-half comeback against Besiktas that reminded him of the glory days against the continent’s elite at Parkhead.

The Premiership champions ran out 3-2 winners thanks to a dramatic 87th-minute clincher from two-goal substitute Camilo Duran and racked up their first points of the campaign to put themselves into 32nd place in the league phase table.

Celtic were a goal down to a Junior Olaitan effort on the rebound after a saved penalty when Duran, Callum Osmand and Colby Donovan were thrown on just after the hour and changed everything.

Osmand levelled with his first touch before Duran put Celtic ahead on 78 minutes. And after Orkun Kokcu had made it 2-2 in the 85th minute with a low drive, Duran popped up three minutes from time to complete a chaotic and badly needed victory.

Manager O’Neill confessed the atmosphere reminded him of his first spell in charge at the turn of the millennium when he led his side to famous wins over the likes of Juventus and Porto and took them to the UEFA Cup final in 2003.

Now, he has ordered his players to concentrate on at least making it into the top 24 of the Europa League and securing a play-off spot.

O'Neill punches the air with delight as his team savour first win in Europa League group

‘I was delighted with the performance,’ said O’Neill. ‘It was fantastic. We put our heart and soul into the game and played some really decent stuff, particularly in the second half.

‘Just when we thought we were going to drop two points, we came roaring back again to win. It was a magnificent effort by the team. So much spirit and heart and desire to go and claw their way not just into the game, but through it.

‘There was a bit of nervousness because we hadn’t a point on the board, but it had everything. We rose to the occasion tonight and what we’ve done is that we’ve given ourselves a chance. We always still think about trying to qualify.

‘Mostly, the crowd give us something and tonight was particularly special. A European night again and it reminded me of the olden days.’

O’Neill also defended his decision to leave Duran, Osmand, Donovan and Haissem Hassan out of the side in favour of the likes of Sebastian Tounekti, struggling record signing Kasper Hogh and Jordan Lotomba, who gifted the penalty-kick that gave Besiktas the lead early in the second period.

Duran , second from left, is hailed by team-mates after scoring winner against Besiktas

‘Lotomba had his first start for us and you are trying to find out as much as you can about players,’ said O’Neill. ‘I made some changes to the side to freshen things up knowing that some of the players — for instance, James Forrest, who was magnificent for us — might not last the game.

‘We had to give the opportunity because we have played a lot of games in relatively quick succession and we go again on Sunday.’

Osmand made a quickfire impression when smashing in a terrific goal from distance after taking a pass from Callum McGregor and has challenged his team-mates to keep delivering the kind of display that turned the game round in the last half-hour.

‘It caught me off guard. I know Cal is good at that reverse (pass) and I am just so glad I caught it nicely,’ said the talented 20-year-old.

‘In my head, I was all jittery and just wanted to come and do something. I want to make something happen and I am so happy with tonight.

A smiling Duran savours the acclaim of Celtic fans after giving the team a 2-1 lead

Osmand helped turn the game around after scoring equaliser with his first touch

‘We did really well to go and win the game. This is what we try to do. The place was rocking at the end and we need to keep bringing these sort of performances and doing well.

‘We have it in us. We have just got to try and keep doing it.’

Osmand also reserved special praise for Colombian hitman Duran in the wake of his matchwinning display.

‘Camilo did amazing. He is such a poacher and scores amazing ones and then poaching ones, so all credit to him,’ he stated.

‘I think the team dug in really well at the start. We stayed strong and got our rewards finally.’

Swedish attacker Benjamin Nygren believes that getting the Europa League campaign back under their own control is hugely important ahead of Celtic’s final four fixtures.

‘We fought very hard and earned the three points in the end. We fought well during the whole game and created enough chances to score more goals,’ said Nygren.

‘This was a very important game and we have it in our own hands with four games to go.

‘We go into every game to win it and we earned it today against a good opponent. We need to continue like this.’

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With no European commitment, De Rossi’s side have been working on the training ground since the 2-1 win against Lecce last weekend. A different story compared to Milan, who faced Ferencvaros on Thursday evening and also lost that game.

Speaking to the media at his press conference yesterday, as transcribed by Calciomercato.com, De Rossi shared his thoughts on the game, Genoa’s current form and the quality of Milan’s team. He warned that they cannot afford to get too cocky.

“We had a little more time to prepare for the match, which is small advantage over Milan. We pushed a little harder, whereas last week we managed the load. We went a little deeper to analyse what we want to do and what we have done.”

Milan have had some high points, but also some setbacks…

“We looked at Milan from a technical and tactical perspective. I evaluate what I see on the pitch, the players they have. And I think they’re among the top three in the league.

“They are very strong and they will fight until the end. Their morale is improving. The derby leaves a positive aftertaste, even though they had a very difficult match on Thursday.”

“Our world is a bit crazy. It swings so fast and we have to keep our feet on the ground. This team always trains well. From our point of view, I like to look ahead, but our goal is to play a good match against Milan. But the moment of protest is recent, and we can’t forget it. We still have a long road ahead.”

“If I didn’t have any ideas two days before the match, it would be worrying (smiles). We are evaluating the technical, physical and mental aspects of our opponents. We are evaluating everything. We have to play a serious game.

“We can’t get too carried away. We are a mid-to-lower-table team, the numbers say it. I don’t want to belittle Genoa, but they are a great team. We have to be aggressive and be aware that we are facing a team that will hurt us if we are too cocky.

“Let’s not forget that Milan beat the strongest team in Italy,” he stated.

Today's Premier League predictions include Manchester United at home to Aston Villa, before struggling Crystal Palace take on Liverpool.

While the Tractor Boys start the next batch of fixtures in 14th position, the Cherries are in eighth place after three successive victories in the top flight.

Liverpool will hope to bounce back and deliver a fatal blow to Pierre Sage's hopes of remaining in charge of Crystal Palace when the two clash in the Premier League on Sunday at Selhurst Park.

Therefore, even a Pedro-less Chelsea side - working on a full week's worth of rest - should stroll to victory, with an increasingly familiar clean sheet in tow.

Desperate to steer clear of the Premier League's relegation zone, Manchester United will host Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

The Red Devils are hoping to build on their midweek Champions League victory, while the Lions are keen to get back on track after a three-game winless run.

Man United may have won in midweek, but they were the beneficiaries of major errors from the Roma defence, and are unlikely to repeat the feat on Sunday.

Villa are on a three-game winless run that has spanned three different competitions, yet they will be optimistic about getting the better of their struggling hosts.

#1654. AC Milan Women 0-3 Inter: Chances squandered and a silly red card

Milan Women failed to replicate the heroics of the men’s team in the Derby della Madonnina, conceding three goals against Inter after a silly red card.

After the odd-goal defeat to Como last night time out, Milan Women were out for revenge this afternoon, and perhaps also a little inspired by the men’s win in the derby last weekend. However, Suzanne Bakker’s side made life very difficult for themselves.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the first half, Milan actually had a couple of good opportunities to take the lead and make it a very different game. After just four minutes, the veteran Christy Grimshaw got a good chance in the box, but failed to connect with the cross from the left with her head from close range.

About ten minutes later, Mawa Sesay picked up on a loose ball after a mistake by Inter’s backline. However, she somehow missed the target and didn’t even force the goalkeeper to a save, effectively squandering a 1v1 by rushing the shot.

In the second half, the game remained fairly even but one moment proved costly for Milan. As Benedetta Glionna made her way into the box, the aforementioned Grimshaw made her evening worse with a little kick, resulting in a penalty for the away side (somewhat cheap, but fair).

Haley Bugeja made no mistakes from the spot, firing a great shot straight down the middle to give her side the lead in the 57th minute. Milan then began their pursuit of an equaliser after that but instead of a goal, around five minutes later, Sandra Ogalla was sent off.

The goalkeeper used her hands a little bit too early, touching the ball outside the penalty box, and the referee immediately spotted it. Bakker made use of the VAR challenge, prompting the referee to have a look at the screen, but the decision was upheld. A silly red card indeed.

Deputy goalkeeper Sally Rainey was brought on but just a few minutes later, Inter doubled their lead through Glionna. It was a well-worked move, in fairness, but the defending could have been better at the far post. That was in the 67th minute.

Milan tried to get back into the game but struggled with only ten players. And so, in the 83rd minute, Inter were awarded another penalty. This one was even cheaper than the first, as Angelica Soffia barely touched the player.

Despite another VAR check, the decision was upheld and Bugeja bagged her second of the night. That concluded the night from a goalscoring point of view, and Milan Women suffered their second consecutive defeat.

#1653. Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their new season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the new season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

Alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

More defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

That goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

Newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

Thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

Then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

Everton have played some quick one and two-touch football around the box in this game, and another move ends with George shooting over the bar. Everton are making their first change: Patterson off, replaced by Rohl.

The game is still finding its shape again after all those Newcastle changes, but Murphy did force a sharp save from Travers with a low shot from a tight angle.

He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

The players on for Newcastle are: Woltemade, Murphy, Willock, Barnes, Ramsey, Johnson, Steur, Pivas, Miley and Charlton.

It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

Everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

A sign of some Newcastle frustration there was Wissa kicks Tyrique George across the shins. A bit naughty that, may even have been worthy of VAR attention in a Premier League game.

The Senegalese sends Hornicek the wrong way and finds the corner. No chance it was a penalty in the first place though, thankfully this is not a competitive game.

This is very soft, there was not much of a challenge by Joelinton on Dewsbury-Hall, but the Everton midfielder goes down in the box and is awarded the penalty.

It really should be 2-0 to Everton, a high-class moving down their left with Armstrong dinking a pass to Barry. He squared to Ndiaye who was free as a bird in the middle, but his shot was too close to Hornicek.

Joelinton runs down a blind alley before lumping a pass out for an Everton throw, and then the Newcastle man fouls Barry. The big Brazilian still finding his legs and getting up to speed.

A moment to forget for both Newcastle centre-backs. Thiaw was bumped and unbalance by Barry, before Botman steps out of defence and kicks fresh air against the Everton forward. Great recovery from Lewis Hall, but the ball breaks for Armstrong, who feeds Barry and he finishes across Hornicek.

Ndiaye has had a quiet start to the game for Everton, but his jinking qualities were on display there to beat a couple of Newcastle defenders. Everton lose the ball in midfield, and Tarkowski makes a superb last-ditch tackle to deny Osula.

Half-hearted appeals for a penalty from Wissa, but Hayden Hackney did not do much wrong. Looks like we will be spared a first-half hydration break, despite it being a sultry evening.

Osula skips through a couple of challenges at the edge of the area but fails to pick a pass in the box. Bazoumana Touré has looked lively for Newcastle on their left flank, and Bamba has done well for them in midfield.

Everton shake themselves into life as an attacking force. Cracking cross from Patterson into the box and Dewsbury-Hall’s run had gone untracked, but he was just stretching and could not generate enough power to beat Hornicek.

Good save from Travers to deny Elanga, but it was Mykolenko who made a hash of things in the box. The left back simply fell over the ball under no pressure. Newcastle the sharper of the two teams so far.

Joelinton feeds Bamba down the left wing for Newcastle who delivers a cross into the penalty area. Keane can only direct his defensive header back towards the penalty spot, but Wissa volleyed over with a first-time hit. Decent chance.

Thierno Barry makes it stick and proves a strong outlet for Everton. Botman brings him down at the expense of a free-kick just beyond the halfway line. Then Wissa drives into the penalty area for Newcastle after a one-two but he fouls Patterson.

Newcastle, playing in their lilac away kit, are the team trying to take the initiative with the ball, but Everton are quite happy staying compact and absorbing pressure. Elanga’s corner delivery is promising, but Osula does not connect cleanly at the back post.

Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

Bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

We know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Big Dunc and Moyes catch up pre-match! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/Jh4APHOZvX

A word that keeps being used about Jaissle is “special”. Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton, Bamba; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula

Newcastle subs: Gillespie, Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Johnson, M Miley, Finneran, Ramsey, Steur, Willock, J Murphy, Barnes, Neave, Woltemade

Your Mags at Murrayfield! ✊ pic.twitter.com/rDXpn0MqCg

Everton XI: Travers; Patterson, Tarkowski, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Deswbury-Hall, Armstrong, Ndiaye; George, Barry

Here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#1652. Sunday’s Bundesliga predictions including FC Koln vs Bayer Leverkusen, Freiburg vs Union Berlin and Hoffenheim vs Schalke 04

By Anthony Nolan | 08 Nov 2026 00:05, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 00:05

Today's Bundesliga predictions will have a major impact at both ends of the table, with Freiburg vying to keep their unlikely title challenge alive against Union Berlin, Bayer Leverkusen battling for Europe at FC Koln, and Schalke 04 desperate for points at Hoffenheim.

Bayer Leverkusen travel to FC Koln's RheinEnergieSTADION on Sunday and will hope to avoid falling behind in the race for a spot in the Bundesliga's top four.

The hosts are 14th in the table with nine points from a possible 24, whereas Leverkusen are in sixth place with 13 points following their 4-2 loss against Stuttgart on October 31.

Leverkusen's form of late has been concerning, though they have been difficult to beat when playing on the road.

Koln have been strong at RheinEnergieSTADION, and while they may struggle to get the better of the visitors, they should have enough to earn a point.

A rebalanced Freiburg will welcome relegation-threatened Union Berlin to Europa-Park Stadion on Sunday, hoping to keep their unlikely Bundesliga title challenge alive.

Die Breisgau-Brasilianer are searching for a fourth win on the bounce, while Die Eisernen are eyeing a first victory in five games.

Freiburg have rediscovered their form after a brief blip, and will be confident of taking all three points against one of the bottom three on Sunday.

However, Union have proven resilient in recent weeks and are unlikely to be easily beaten, so expect a close contest.

Relegation-threatened Schalke 04 will travel to SNP Arena on Sunday, hoping to catch floundering Bundesliga opponents Hoffenheim off guard before the international break.

Die Kraichgauer are looking for a first win in four games, while Die Knappen are desperate to avoid a fifth defeat in six matches.

Hoffenheim have struggled once again in recent weeks, but they will be quietly confident about their chances of beating one of the division's relegation favourites on Sunday.

Schalke's troubles in front of goal are well-documented, and it would be a surprise to see them find the back of the net, never mind walk away with anything from this clash.

#1651. Report: Liverpool launch recruitment mission for Alisson successor

Liverpool's number one spot has been undisputed for close to a decade.

When Alisson arrived from Roma for a then world record fee for a goalkeeper it was clear that the club felt they had found their man.

The Brazilian has one of the very best 'keepers in the world during his time at Anfield, and there has never been any doubt over his position in the squad.

The 34-year-old is now into the final months of his deal and is currently set to leave Merseyside for free in the summer.

Replacing him will be a priority, and the Reds are already reportedly putting the work in.

Liverpool eyeing Alisson replacementIt will be no easy task succeeding one of the greatest goalkeepers the Premier League has ever seen, but the Reds need to find the man for the job. Giorgi Mamardashvili will be an obvious contender, with the Georgian already at the club, and Lucca Brughmans is another option, with the 18-year-old signed for a substantial fee last summer before returning to Genk on loan. A fresh report has now suggested that Liverpool could turn to the transfer market once again to fill the void left by Alisson however.

It will be no easy task succeeding one of the greatest goalkeepers the Premier League has ever seen, but the Reds need to find the man for the job.

Giorgi Mamardashvili will be an obvious contender, with the Georgian already at the club, and Lucca Brughmans is another option, with the 18-year-old signed for a substantial fee last summer before returning to Genk on loan.

A fresh report has now suggested that Liverpool could turn to the transfer market once again to fill the void left by Alisson however.

According to Football Insider, Liverpool have set their sights on Brighton 'keeper Bart Verbruggen ahead of the summer transfer window.

The Dutchman, who has been on the radar at Anfield for quite some time, has admirers from all round Europe but Liverpool could be the ones to tempt him away from the Amex.

The 24-year-old has already recorded six clean sheets in nine Premier League appearances this season, and has been a huge part of the Seagulls early season success.

Real Madrid are also reported as a potential suitor for Verbruggen should he leave Brighton, and although no price tag is mentioned by Football Insider it would likely take a hefty fee to secure his services.

Valued at €46.6 million (~£39m) by FootballTransfers, the Netherlands international is entering the final 18 months of his deal and Brighton could be tempted to cash in.

If Alisson does move on from Merseyside this summer then Verbruggen could be the man in line to take his place.

#1650. Opposition insight for Genoa-Milan: Form, injuries, predicted XI and more

Genoa are the next opponents for AC Milan and given the Rossoblu’s recent form, they certainly could have faced them at a better time.

Ruben Amorim and his men really need to pick themselves up with a win tomorrow afternoon, which would at least allow them to build on the derby win in the league. In the Europa League, however, that chance is already gone as they lost to Ferencvaros.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, getting the three points might not be the easiest task as Genoa have been in red-hot form lately, and will certainly use all of the support from their fans at the Marassi tomorrow.

➤ Manager: Daniele De Rossi ➤ Form (all comps): W-L-W-W-W (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Serie A): Osmajic – 4 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Colombo and El Shaarawy – 2 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: None.

After what was a disastrous start to the 2025-26 season under Patrick Vieira, sitting rock bottom between the 7th and 9th matchdays, Daniele De Rossi was appointed. He quickly brought them above the relegation zone and managed to keep them there, finishing seven points clear in the end.

It was only right to confirm him for this season, as such, and there have been no regrets so far. The start was admittedly dodgy, with one draw and four defeats in the first five games, but there have been four wins and one defeat in the five games since. Crisis very much averted.

The only defeat in the last five games came against De Rossi’s former club as well, namely Roma, who have been on fire at the start of this season. There can be no accusations of the former midfielder throwing the game to benefit his former club, let’s put it that way.

Nevertheless, the poor star has been cancelled out and it’s possible that De Rossoneri just needed some time, especially after losing key players like Jeff Ekhator (to Juventus) and Brooke Norton-Vuffy (to Hull City). The Serie A veteran Ruslan Malinovskyi also waved goodbye as his contract expired.

On the flip side, the Rossoblu did keep hold of most of the key players from last season, such as Johan Vasquez, Leo Ostigard, Morten Frendrup, and Lorenzo Colombo. The latter was bought permanently from Milan after a season-long loan, as the conditions for the obligation were triggered.

Some interesting signings were also made, from the veteran (and former Milan man) Stephan El Shaarawy to the familiar face Hamed Traore, who played for Sassuolo between 2019 and 2013. After spells at Bournemouth, Napoli, Auxerre and Marseille, he’s now looking to regain stability.

As for the latest team news, De Rossi has a much better situation than Amorim with no injuries or suspensions to note. Lorenzo Venturino and Elias Havel were both on the sidelines but have returned for this one.

It looks like the former Milan men El Shaarawy and Colombo will start, while Junior Messias could perhaps be introduced from the bench. De Rossi didn’t give much away during his presser in terms of the team selection, but did make sure to express his respect for the Rossoneri.

Genoa (3-5-2): Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ellertsson, Baldanzi, Frendrup, Traore, El Shaarawy; Colombo, Osmajic.

Predicted bench: Stolz, Sommariva, Messias, Otoa, Sabelli, Puczka, Amorim, Meichtry, Mitaj, Vitinha, Sow, Drameh, Ehizibue, Wiafe, Venturino, Havel.

#1649. CELTIC 3 BESIKTAS 2: Duran and Osmand make the difference from the bench as O'Neill's men roar back to claim precious victory

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:33 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 18:56 EDT, 5 November 2026

By the time the Celtic players had reacquainted themselves with the concept of a lap of honour on a European night, those who had come to decry the club’s hierarchy had shuffled off into the night.

This somewhat unexpected outcome saved Martin O’Neill from the ignominy of being the first manager in the history of the Parkhead club to suffer five straight losses in European competition.

It should also lower the temperature in the ongoing feud between the directors and the fanbase for a few days at least.

After a diabolical start to their Europa League campaign, O’Neill’s men are belatedly up and running. The task of accruing sufficient points to reach the knock-out round again is still enormous although it is not yet beyond them. There’s life in this yet.

Of the four sides who Celtic were drawn to play in Glasgow in this phase, Besiktas looked the most imposing. In taking their scalp, O’Neill’s side will have received a much-needed infusion of self-belief. An inexorable slide towards a full-blown crisis has been avoided, for now.

This was quite the night. A drab and goalless first half was no indication of what was to come.

Camilo Duran squeezes home the winner in the 87th minute for Celtic

Substitutes Callum Osmand (left) and Camilo Duran turned the tide for Celtic

O’Neill’s men fell behind through a penalty but, to their enormous credit, they did not wilt.

So much of the credit for a famous triumph belonged to two players who, oddly, didn’t start the match.

Callum Osmand levelled with his first touch and was scintillating in everything he did from that point on.

Camilo Duran, another who’d started the night clad in a tracksuit, edged O’Neill’s side in front following a majestic ball from Osmand.

When Besiktas levelled with five minutes remaining, many of the home supporters would probably have settled for a draw. Not a bit of it. Duran’s second of the night, two minutes later, secured a magnificent victory, one which might just prove to be a turning point.

For those arriving in the stadium and checking their phones, O’Neill’s team selection required a second take. After playing just 31 minutes across three substitute appearances, Jordan Lotomba was handed his first start at right back ahead of Colby Donovan.

James Forrest and Sebastian Tounekti were deployed on the flanks with Kasper Hogh selected in place of Duran at centre-forward. So much for a must-win game.

There was familiarity in the Besiktas side in the shape of former Rangers winger Vaclav Cerny and Oh Hyeon-gyu, formerly a striker in this parish.

Although the Turks controlled the first half, Celtic did fashion the first real opening. Mika Baur fed Tounekti who squared the ball to Benjamin Nygren. The Swede ought to have done much better than fire wildly over.

Celtic’s attempt to press high was admirable. All too often, though, the men in black just played through it.

Forrest did well to move the ball on and invited Lotomba to attack it. He was easily brushed aside.

Duran celebrates making it 2-1 in a thrilling second half at Parkhead

It became a recurring theme. Not only were Besiktas technically superior to Celtic in the opening half, collectively, they were physically stronger. If there was a 50/50 to be won, invariably, they won it.

The upshot was that O’Neill’s men made little headway when they got into promising positions.

It said much that the biggest roar of the first half from the home supporters came when Liam Scales took ball then man – that man being Cerny.

You had to wonder what instructions Sam Johnstone had been given. His tactic of launching the ball long to Hogh was, to say the least, optimistic. With next to nothing coming from the flanks, the Dane was again starved of service.

The encouraging thing for O’Neill at the break was the fact that Besiktas’ possession hadn’t translated into too many chances. Cerny fired over. Leandro Trossard forced Johnstone into a good stop, although the offside flag had been raised.

Tounekti contributed another uninspiring display. Time and again, he gathered the ball on the flank. If there was an easy option to take, he took it.

The Tunisian had a chance to play Forrest in after creeping infield. Remarkably, he managed to stumble on the ball and Besiktas sprang another attack.

Although Celtic were level at the break, they’d been feckless. A chance to fashion something from a free-kick saw Tounekti pick out Nygren. The Swede completely lost his footing and the chance was gone.

Callum McGregor was the most relieved man in the ground in the opening seconds of the second period. He turned into trouble on the edge of his own box in the shape of Junior Olaitan and watched as Trossard’s curler flew just over.

Another old head in Forrest came close at the other end, his slalom from right to centre ending with a low shot which the keeper fielded.

Lotomba’s display throughout was poor, entirely in keeping with a player with so little football under his belt.

Osmand made an instant impact in rifling home for 1-1 from the edge of the box

It was no surprise that the error which led to Besiktas’ opener came from him. Johnstone created the initial problem by needlessly smashing a clearance off the frame of Trossard. It broke kindly to Ernest Poku. With no need to panic, Lotomba did exactly that. His scything of his opponent was a clear penalty.

Johnstone stood up to block Olaitan’s initial effort but couldn’t recover in time. The Besiktas man smashed home the rebound once the ball had fallen from the night sky. It was scarcely ill-deserved at that point.

O’Neill threw on Duran, Osmand and Donovan. The changes yielded an immediate return.

Advanced on the left of the box, McGregor showed composure to square the ball to Osmand. Any fears of ring-rust from the substitute were misplaced. A crisp right-foot shot flew into the bottom corner to level.

Credit where it’s due. Having hardly worried the Turks up to that stage, Celtic found something. Scales had his head in his hands after being denied a headed goal from a corner by a smart save by Alexander Nobel in the Besiktas goal.

With Osmand’s work rate giving the home fans something to get behind, Celtic improved. Another surge by the forward brought Hogh into the game. Duran’s pace took him into a dangerous position but the Dane couldn’t find him.

Osmand then fed the advanced Nygren. Again, the normally dependable Swede didn’t have his shooting boots on.

The former Fulham player seemed to be everywhere. It was his brilliantly measured pass which cut the Turkish defence wide open as Celtic turned the game on its head with 78 minutes remaining.

Perfectly weighted and angled, it still asked a lot of Duran. The Colombian did brilliantly, gathering and rounding the keeper in the blink of an eye then rolling the ball into an empty net.

As Celtic Park rejoiced, substitute Haissem Hassan fizzed one into the keeper’s arms.

How O’Neill’s men would come to rue that moment. There didn’t appear to be much on when substitute Orkun Kokcu took aim 25 yards out and thundered the ball low past Johnstone.

A slow burner of a game had certainly sprang into life. And we weren’t done yet.

Celtic dusted themselves down and came again. Donovan motored across the field and found Tierney. The full-back’s strike didn’t have the power to trouble the keeper but fell kindly for Duran. At the second attempt, he bundled the ball home.

#1648. Sunday's La Liga predictions including Atletico Madrid vs. Barcelona, Elche vs. Real Betis

By Ben Sully | 08 Nov 2026 00:10, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 00:10

Today's La Liga predictions include Barcelona's clash against title rivals Atletico Madrid, and Real Betis' away meeting with Elche.

Real Betis will aim to make it successive wins in Spain's top flight when they continue their campaign against Elche at Estadio Martinez Valero on Sunday afternoon.

The visitors posted a 2-1 victory over Malaga in their last league match, while Elche will enter the contest off the back of a 1-0 home defeat to Valencia.

Elche have been in solid form of late, and this is not a straightforward match for Real Betis, but we are backing the Seville outfit to secure a valuable three points on Sunday.

Paris have struggled to replicate their home performances on the road, and Sinayoko's potential absence could leave Rosenior's men settling for a point.

Real Sociedad will look to extend their three-game unbeaten home run when they take on Rayo Vallecano in Sunday's La Liga encounter at Anoeta.

The Basque side start the weekend in fifth spot in La Liga, while the visitors are sitting in 12th position in the standings.

While Real Sociedad have found life difficult in recent meetings with Rayo, they come into this one on the back of consecutive home wins, and we think they will make full use of home advantage to get the better of a Rayo side that has lost three of their five away league games this term.

> Real Sociedad vs. Rayo Vallecano preview

Both Celta Vigo and Levante will be bidding to return to winning ways in Spain's top flight when they lock horns in Vigo on Sunday evening.

Celta will enter the match off the back of a 2-1 home defeat to Union SG in the Europa League, while Levante suffered a 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid in the league last time out.

Home advantage could be key in this match; we are expecting it to be tight in terms of the scoreline, but Celta should be able to navigate their way to all three points.

Villarreal will be bidding to bounce back from a heavy European defeat when they continue their La Liga campaign against Getafe on Sunday.

The Yellow Submarine suffered a 6-0 loss to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League last time out, while Getafe were beaten 1-0 by Brighton & Hove Albion in the Conference League.

Villarreal will have had longer to prepare for this match due to Getafe's European commitments on Thursday, and we are expecting the Yellow Submarine to navigate their way to all three points.

One of the biggest matches on the Spanish football calendar will take place at the Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday night, as Atletico Madrid host Barcelona in La Liga.

It is a meeting between the top two in the La Liga table, with Barca currently at the summit on 30 points, while Atletico are second on 28 points.

This is such a difficult match to call; we came close to backing a draw - either 1-1 or 2-2 - but have ultimately settled on a narrow success for the reigning champions.
